# Independent audit: Gaussian sequence archives over polynomial ellipsoids

Date: 7 October 2026. Auditor: `gaussian_sequence_audit`.

**Finding.** The claimed retained-memory order passes an independent reconstruction in the exact measurable-channel model. Both bounds are uniform in the amplitude `A`, with constants depending only on the fixed smoothness exponent. The lower can use a fixed transformation `tanh X` and an explicit bounded proper loss, giving

\[
 \ln D\ge \frac d2\ln\frac r\epsilon
              -\left(\frac54+\ln 2\right)d,
 \qquad 0<r\le1.
 \tag{1}
\]

Only the `2d` means `+/-r e_i` are needed for this inequality; preserving the null law is not an extra lower-bound premise. The upper is a finite coordinate partition followed by a null-conditional Gaussian decoder. It does not rely on N30, fixed-dimension constants, or a quantum-to-Gaussian bridge.

The result is an information-theoretic theorem for continuous-output random kernels. It is not a finite-running-time theorem for a machine that returns finitely many bits: such output is countably supported and has TV distance one from a continuous Gaussian. Generating the whole countable sequence also requires infinite output and an ideal source of fresh randomness. Those resources must be explicit. This audit is internal mathematical evidence, not external correctness certification or historical novelty clearance.

## 1. Exact interface and theorem

The observation space is the standard Borel product

\[
 \Omega=\mathbb R^{\mathbb N},\qquad
 P_\theta=\bigotimes_{j\ge1}N(\theta_j,1).
\]

The supplied mean class is

\[
 \Theta_{\alpha,A}
  =\left\{\theta:\sum_{j\ge1}j^{2\alpha}\theta_j^2\le A^2\right\},
 \qquad \alpha>0,  A>0.
 \tag{2}
\]

Every such mean is in `ell_2`. The coordinate system, covariance, exponent, amplitude and requested tolerance are supplied public model inputs. The encoder receives one draw `X`, not the unknown `theta`.

The archive is a finite quantum memory, or a hybrid direct sum of total Hilbert dimension

\[

\]

Every retained input-dependent register and classical branch counts. The decoder is a parameter-independent POVM/random kernel with output `Y in Omega`; it cannot revisit `X`. # Gaussian weak-signal archives: a dimension-uniform upper construction

Date: 2026-10-07. Status: complete internal derivation under the statistical-kernel interface below; external correctness and priority review remain open. The supplied N30 summary was read, but its missing proof was not used as a premise. This construction uses hats linear in the original Gaussian coordinate on a Cauchy-spaced grid, rather than claiming to have recovered N30's hats linear in the Cauchy coordinate.

## Result and interface

Write `P_t=N(t,1)` and use TV equal to half L1. There is an absolute finite constant `K`, independent of all dimensions and signals, such that for every integer `J>=1` there is a blind classical archive with at most `J` labels and output law `Q_t` satisfying, simultaneously for `|t|<=1`,

\[
Q_0=P_0,\qquad
\chi^2(Q_t\Vert P_t)\le K t^2 J^{-4},\qquad
\operatorname{TV}(Q_t,P_t)\le \frac{\sqrt K}{2}|t|J^{-2}.
\tag{1}
\]

The encoder sees one Gaussian observation, not `t`. The decoder receives the retained label and outputs a fresh real observation through a parameter-independent stochastic kernel. The supplied model, `J`, and decoder program are input-independent. All input-dependent records are discarded except the label. No entangled receiver reference or other input-dependent side record is used. Independent seeds are unnecessary.

Consequently, tensoring the same channel independently across `d` coordinates gives, for every mean vector with `max_i |theta_i|<=1`,

\[
Q^{(d)}_\theta=\bigotimes_i Q_{\theta_i},\qquad
\operatorname{TV}(Q^{(d)}_\theta,N(\theta,I_d))
\le \sqrt{K/2}\,\|\theta\|_2 J^{-2}.
\tag{2}
\]

Thus for `0<r<=1`, on the full Euclidean ball `||theta||_2<=r` and hence on `{0,+/-r e_i}` or its `k`-sparse subball, one can attain error `epsilon` with

\[
\log_2D\le \frac d2\log_2(r/\epsilon)+O(d)
\tag{3}
\]

when `epsilon/r` is small. The constant in `O(d)` is absolute. There is no dimension-dependent tail allocation and no `sqrt(k)` penalty. Inactive coordinates are reconstructed **exactly** as null Gaussians; the retained alphabet nevertheless contains all coordinate labels because the encoder is blind to the active direction.

The stronger chi-square statement in (1), rather than coordinatewise TV addition, is what removes the sparse-support factor. If `epsilon >= r/sqrt(2pi)`, the one-label null decoder already works; (3) is not a claim
